youtube.baslik: Educating Children with Hearing Loss: Inclusion | Lesson 270 | AIHEAR Audiology Academy
youtube.aciklama:
How is a child with hearing loss supported at school? In this lesson we cover inclusive education in Türkiye, the RAM and BEP process, classroom acoustics criteria, seating, remote microphones, informing the teacher and the audiologist's work with the school.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: Ministry of National Education, Special Education Services Regulation, Türkiye (2018); Eurydice, Türkiye: Special education provision in primary and secondary schools (2025); ANSI/ASA S12.60-2010/Part 1, Acoustical Performance Criteria, Design Requirements, and Guidelines for Schools; ASHA, Guidelines for Addressing Acoustics in Educational Settings (2005); American Academy of Audiology, Clinical Practice Guidelines: Remote Microphone Hearing Assistance Technologies for Children and Youth from Birth to 21 Years (2008); Anderson, Screening Instrument for Targeting Educational Risk (SIFTER).

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

sahneler.baslik: Children with hearing loss: *inclusion* and the classroom
sahneler.alt: IEP, classroom acoustics, seating, the teacher
cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson we will look at school life for a child with hearing loss, inclusion in Türkiye and the individualized education program.
We will also cover classroom acoustics, seating, remote microphones and informing the teacher.

maddeler.metin: At most two students per class
Special schools are also an option

cumleler: Inclusive education means a student with special needs learning in the same class as peers, with the support needed.
In Türkiye, the Ministry of National Education's Special Education Services Regulation calls this inclusion or integration.
In this setting, materials, teaching methods and assessment are adapted to the student's needs.
The core principle is the least restrictive educational environment; for many students with hearing loss, this is a mainstream school.
According to Ministry sources, students in inclusion are placed so that there are at most two in one class.
There are also day or boarding special schools for students with hearing loss; the choice depends on the child's needs.
The process begins by documenting the hearing loss and the technology used in a clear report.
The Guidance and Research Center, known as RAM, carries out the child's educational assessment and recommends the best setting.
The child is placed in a school and class in line with this recommendation.
A school with a student in inclusion forms a unit to develop the individualized education program, called BEP in Türkiye.
When needed, extra teaching can be given one to one or in a small group in a resource room.
Because the regulations are updated from time to time, details should be checked each year in the Ministry's current texts.

cumleler.yazi: The individualized education program, or IEP, is a written education plan specific to the student.
cumleler.ses: The individualized education program, or I E P, is a written education plan specific to the student.

cumleler: The program starts by describing the student's present performance, strengths and needs.
Then long and short-term educational goals are written.

cumleler.yazi: For a student with hearing loss, supports such as a remote microphone, seating and visual aids are written into the IEP.
cumleler.ses: For a student with hearing loss, supports such as a remote microphone, seating and visual aids are written into the I E P.

cumleler: Adaptations such as extra time in exams, a quiet room and written instructions may also be part of the program.

cumleler.yazi: In the IEP unit, school administrators, the school counselor, class and subject teachers and the parent work together.
cumleler.ses: In the I E P unit, school administrators, the school counselor, class and subject teachers and the parent work together.

cumleler: The program is reviewed at regular intervals; new goals are written as goals are reached.

sahneler.baslik: Why is the classroom a *hard* place?
cumleler: Classroom acoustics covers how noise, reverberation and distance in a classroom affect understanding speech.
The teacher's voice reaches the student by a direct path, but sound reflected from the walls, ceiling and floor also arrives.
Reflections that arrive quickly strengthen the sound; if they last long, they smear syllables together.
Chair noise, hallway noise and ventilation noise also mix with these reflections.
Children struggle more than adults in noise because their language and listening skills are still developing.
For a child with hearing loss the difficulty is even greater; the device amplifies nearby noise along with the teacher's voice.

cumleler.yazi: In the US, the American National Standards Institute's classroom acoustics standard is a widely cited reference.
cumleler.ses: In the U S, the American National Standards Institute's classroom acoustics standard is a widely cited reference.

cumleler.yazi: Under this standard, background noise in an empty, furnished classroom should not exceed 35 dBA.
cumleler.ses: Under this standard, background noise in an empty, furnished classroom should not exceed thirty five decibels A.

cumleler: In classrooms up to about 283 cubic meters, reverberation time should be no more than 0.6 seconds.
In larger classrooms the limit is 0.7 seconds.
The American Speech-Language-Hearing Association recommends the teacher's voice be 15 decibels or more above noise at the child's ear.
Many real classrooms do not meet these values, so acoustic treatment and a remote microphone are considered together.
Sitting near the teacher keeps the child in the zone where direct sound is stronger than reflected sound.
The distance where direct and reflected sound are equal is called the critical distance; the front rows are closest to the direct sound.
The child is seated away from noise sources such as windows, the hallway door, the projector and ventilation.
In a child with unilateral or asymmetric loss, the better ear should face the teacher and the class.
The front center seat is not always best; the child should be able to turn slightly to see classmates too.
A U-shaped seating layout makes it easier for the child to see both the teacher and the faces of classmates who speak.
In a remote microphone system, the teacher wears a microphone close to the mouth; we saw how it works in the wireless audio lesson.
The teacher's voice goes directly to the child's device, largely overcoming distance and reverberation.
In class discussions, a second microphone passed from hand to hand also brings classmates' voices to the child.
The teacher, or an older child, confirms each day with a short listening check that the system works.

cumleler.yazi: The audiologist fits and verifies the system with the device; the American Academy of Audiology's 2008 guideline describes these steps.
cumleler.ses: The audiologist fits and verifies the system with the device; the American Academy of Audiology's two thousand eight guideline describes these steps.

cumleler: The microphone should be muted when the teacher talks privately with a student or leaves the classroom.
The teacher faces the class while speaking; not talking while writing on the board preserves both speechreading and sound.
Questions and answers from classmates are briefly repeated by the teacher.
Key words, instructions and homework are written on the board or on paper.
Captions are turned on for videos watched in class.
Instead of asking did you understand, having the child say what was explained in their own words gives more accurate information.
The teacher knows the basic check for the device and remote microphone, and whom to contact if there is a problem.
Studying the key words of a new topic before the lesson, or preteaching, makes the lesson easier for the child to follow.
Listening and taking notes at the same time is hard; a classmate's notes or the teacher's lesson summary can help.

cumleler.yazi: Extra time in exams and homework is one of the adaptations that can be set out in the IEP.
cumleler.ses: Extra time in exams and homework is one of the adaptations that can be set out in the I E P.

cumleler: Taking exams in a quiet room instead of a noisy classroom may also be considered.
For foreign language listening exams, direct audio streaming to the device or a written alternative is considered.
Which adaptations are needed is decided with the team according to the child's needs.
Inclusion is not only about academic success; making friends and joining in play matter at least as much.
Listening with intense attention all day is tiring; fatigue and reduced attention may appear by the end of the day.
With the consent of the child and family, an age-appropriate talk about hearing and devices can be given to the class.
As the child grows, they learn to tell the teacher about their needs themselves, in other words self-advocacy.
Meeting peers who use hearing aids or implants, and Deaf young people, also supports identity development.
The school should also watch for signs of exclusion and bullying and stay in contact with the family.

adimlar.metin: At the start of each year

cumleler: The audiologist gives the school a short report and a list of recommendations in plain language the teacher can understand.
Fitting and verifying the device and remote microphone is the audiologist's responsibility.
Teacher and student questionnaires show the child's listening difficulties in class; the SIFTER is one such questionnaire.
When possible, the audiologist meets the teacher; observing the class makes sure the advice fits real conditions.
At the start of each school year, the new teacher is informed and the technology is checked again.
The report highlights what the child needs in class rather than diagnostic details.

sahneler.metin: Give the teacher a one-page note: the child's device, seating, how to use the remote microphone and a number to call if there is a problem.
cumleler: A clinical tip: give the teacher a one-page information note instead of a long report.
The note should include the child's device, the recommended seat and how to use the remote microphone.
Also add contact details the teacher can use if there is a problem.
Update this note at the start of each school year, because the teacher and class may change.

maddeler.metin: RAM assesses; the school prepares the IEP

cumleler: Inclusion means a child with hearing loss learning in the same class as peers, with the needed support and adaptations.
In Türkiye, RAM carries out the educational assessment, and the school's BEP unit prepares the individualized program.
In the classroom, noise and reverberation are reduced, the child sits near the teacher and a remote microphone is used.
Informing the teacher and the audiologist's regular work with the school determine the success of inclusion.

sahneler.soru: What is the minimum recommended signal-to-noise ratio?
sahneler.aciklama: The teacher's voice should be _at least 15 dB_ above the noise.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: what is the minimum signal-to-noise ratio recommended in class for a child with hearing loss?

cumleler: The correct answer is C: plus 15 decibels.
Since many classrooms do not reach this value, acoustic treatment and a remote microphone are used together.
